messages:
incident-bot: [PAGER] CONTINUOUS_BATCHING_LATENCY_SPIKE - p95 token latency > 3s across region-us-east-1 for last 3m. Error rate: 5xx 1.2%, 429 3.5%. Routing: dedicated pools + hosted fallbacks. Pager severity: high.
oncall-maya: ack. I'm on it, paging rotation is me. Starting triage.
oncall-maya: quick context: we rolled the adaptive microbatcher change last night (batch_cap=256 -> adaptive), traffic ramped at 09:12 UTC; seeing a sustained high-concurrency waveform ~9k concurrent.
devon: logs look like KV cache bloom — eviction thrashing, >60% cache miss rate, heavy KV evictions triggered continuous batch assembly churn.
sam: observed microbatch sizes collapsing to 1-3 tokens repeatedly, causing many small GPU invocations. That combined with queue jitter means per-request latency skyrockets.
oncall-maya: ok, combined failure mode: at high concurrency, adaptive batcher shrinks batches due to jitter/latency feedback loop -> KV cache keys proliferate (prefix churn) -> eviction thrash -> batcher sees cache misses -> more tiny batches.
nina: impact: customers with long-context streaming (acme-inc, finpay) seeing 4-7x latency and elevated 429s. CS Zoe is in loop.
cs-zoe: pinged impacted accounts, flagged high-urgency. Finpay wants an ETA, reporting degraded SLAs for certain routes.
patrick: going to attempt emergency hotfix: temporarily cap batcher min_size=8 and increase jitter-smoothing window. Rolling to a small % now.
oncall-maya: do not roll to global yet. Let's patch dedicated pools first and monitor. Who can run the rollout?
devon: I can push canary to dedicated-us-east-1 now. Command: ```./infractl rollout --service=continuous-batcher --env=dedicated-us-east-1 --set=batcher.min_size=8 --set=batcher.jitter_window_ms=200```
ops-bot: Started rollout job #7853 to dedicated-us-east-1 (canary).
patrick: canary up, metrics: p95 down from 3.8s -> 1.4s on canary hosts within 90s, 429s down 60%. KV miss still elevated but stabilizing.
oncall-maya: good. Promote to all dedicated pools in us-east and us-west, leave hosted untouched for now.
devon: promoting... ops-bot: Rolling out to 8 hosts in us-east, 6 hosts in us-west. Progress: 40% -> 100%.
ops-bot: Rollout complete to dedicated pools.
nina: monitoring customer metrics. Finpay: latency down to ~1.6s but still degraded for long-stream routes at tail. Acme-inc reporting significantly improved.
oncall-maya: Next step: implement KV eviction smoothing and prefix coalescing to avoid bloom. That's a code change and will take more time. For immediate live mitigation we'll: 1) cap adaptive shrink threshold 2) increase throttle on hosted fallback to reduce extra load 3) enable temporary rate-limit per-token for top noisy customers.
devon: filed PR #7892 (hotfix) to add batcher.shrink_backoff_ms and prefix-coalesce toggle. Testing now.
sam: also seeing a correlated spike in CPU on controller that queues batches; added a temporary CPU affinity limit to the controller to prioritize batch commit loop. Deployed to canary.
oncall-maya: Customer impact summary for Pager: Affected: acme-inc (high), finpay (critical), notebookly (medium). Visible symptoms: p95 token latency up 3-7x, 429 increase, some streaming sessions reset. Mitigation: canary->global hotfix reduced p95 ~2x and 429s ~60% for dedicated customers. Hosted users partially impacted; plan limited rollout to hosted in 20m if metrics hold.
cs-zoe: relayed to finpay: root cause under investigation, immediate mitigations rolling, ETA for full fix ~3-6 hours; offered credits and workaround (pin to older model version).
patrick: note — if we see re-bloom after promotion, we'll temporarily reduce concurrency cap for affected pools to 6k and force sticky routing to stable model variants.
oncall-maya: agree. Also schedule a follow-up postmortem and a regression test covering high concurrency + adaptive batcher toggles.
devon: test harness task filed: loadgen scenario 'concurrency-lattice' to reproduce microburst + jitter.
ops-bot: Alert: hosted-us-east fallback rate limit triggered, dropping new requests at 10% rate.
sam: I'm increasing hosted rate-limit to allow more burst handling but keeping per-customer throttle. Command: ```./infractl config set hosted.rate_limit_burst=1500```
patrick: caution — raising hosted burst could propagate load back; keep close watch.
oncall-maya: agreed. We keep hosted small increases only. Nina, continue customer comms. Zoe, update Finpay when hosted rollout begins.
cs-zoe: done. Finpay acknowledged workaround; asked for notification when fully resolved.
ina: current metrics (10m post-rollout): dedicated p95 1.3s -> trending to 900ms, 429s down to baseline+0.2%. Hosted still at p95 ~2.2s. KV eviction rate: down 45% on dedicated, hosted 20% improvement.
oncall-maya: handing off to second-line oncall @devon for monitoring and follow-up. My shift ends in 25m. Key follow-ups: finish PR #7892, schedule postmortem, add e2e regression, confirm hosted rollout only when KV eviction metrics stable for 30m.
devon: taking handoff. Will run extra canaries and watch for re-bloom. If re-bloom, immediate action: revert adaptive change and force batch_cap=256.
ops-bot: Handoff recorded: incident thread 3519876543 -> oncall rotation devon.
incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> partial (dedicated mitigated, hosted partial). Severity remains high until hosted restored.
oncall-maya: thanks team. If anyone sees new 5xx/429 spikes tag me and devon. :thumbsup:
patrick: adding follow-up ticket to infra backlog for smarter KV prefix coalescing and adaptive batcher safety nets. Ticket: INFRA-4473.
devon: will write up timeline and initial notes in incidents/ and include metric graphs.
cs-zoe: will follow up with impacted customers and collect post-incident feedback.
patrick: end of thread.
